headline: Kuaishou's AI video service Kling is reported to be heading for a Hong Kong share listing while it still loses money.
score_reason: Lowered from 5 by 1: the listing plan was reported on 6 Oct 2026 and the funding and buyback terms were published in July, so this article mostly restates earlier news with context.
importance_line: What changed is only added detail on the money behind a possible listing, which matters first to investors who may be offered shares, then to Kuaishou and rival AI video makers such as ByteDance's Seedance, and the doubt is that the listing is an unconfirmed plan, the loss figures come from unnamed market sources and the timing could slip.
source: Sina Finance, citing Phoenix WEEKLY Finance
summary: Sina Finance, drawing on interviews by Phoenix WEEKLY Finance, reports that Kling AI, the AI video generator of the Chinese short-video company Kuaishou, is expected to seek a Hong Kong listing, following Bloomberg's report of 6 Oct 2026 that banks were chosen for a sale raising at least $1 billion, and that outside investors in July 2026 valued it at up to $18 billion (over 120 billion yuan). Kling still makes a loss on first-half 2026 revenue of over 1.5 billion yuan, and under the July terms investors can demand their money back with 8 percent yearly interest if it has not listed by 30 Oct 2031, which one analyst quoted calls a bargaining chip rather than an immediate pressure.
notes: Follows our 6 Oct 2026 edition item on Kling picking banks (Bloomberg). Pool follow_up flag was false; set here from our own archive. Read in Chinese on Sina Finance (the long URL with tracking codes was cleaned; text first read via the decoded Google link) and cross-checked with OFweek. The article appears to rest on Phoenix WEEKLY Finance interviews; the exact original author is not clear, so the credit is Sina Finance, citing Phoenix WEEKLY Finance.
